goal: Implement the Supervisor's four-gate acceptance loop end to end so a task can go Worker -> G1 -> G2 -> commit -> PR -> G3 -> G4 -> merge with evidence at every step, and a failing task can never reach merged.
requirements: G1/G2/G3/G4 are task metadata AND an executor: `rddev task verify|accept|reject` drive them, and each gate records its evidence (commands, exit status, output) so the chain Requirement -> Task -> Worker -> RESULT -> Verification -> Commit -> PR -> Merge -> Tests is reconstructible from disk.
Supervisor can accept, reject, rework (same worker) or respawn (new worker); a rejected task records the rejection evidence.
After acceptance, ONLY the Supervisor performs commit/push/PR/merge - and the tooling must refuse any of those steps when a blocking gate is red.
Support an independent Review Worker (no Git control-plane) and record its verdict as evidence.

REQUIRED: detect a self-contradictory RESULT at collect - one that claims status completed while a required test is not_run, or whose summary/payload says it is an interim snapshot. A previous worker did exactly this and shipped a false completion; the check must be mechanical, not a human reading it.

REQUIRED: G2 must run the CI workflow's EXACT steps, and the merge gate must assert EVERY required job is green rather than grepping for one check name. The Supervisor merged a red PR once because G2 ran a similar-looking subset; the runner must make that impossible.

REQUIRED: validate every allowed_scope glob against the real file tree before dispatch, and require that a task whose scope covers a marker input (specs/**, tasks/tasks.json) also covers the derived artifacts it necessarily changes (specs/SPEC_VERSION.json). Three separate tasks were blocked or falsely rejected because the Supervisor wrote a scope narrower than the work required.
Reuse T0011's collect-time invariants (HEAD==baseline, refs, allowed_scope diff, RESULT schema, host residue) rather than re-implementing them.

REQUIRED (security review, confirmed by inspection): the GATE INPUTS must not be Worker-writable. spawn writes task-package.json (the source of allowed_scope) and registry.json (the source of baseline_sha) into .rddev/workers/<TASK>/, which is the Worker's own result dir - and the guard's write allow-list explicitly permits that dir. A Worker can therefore widen its own allowed_scope or rewrite its recorded baseline_sha, defeating the two central collect invariants. Move the authoritative gate inputs outside the Worker's write allow-list (the guard permits only the worktree, $POST_WORKER_RESULT_DIR and /tmp, so any other path is already off-limits) and have collect read them from there. Also consider the same vector for the generated guard and settings files in that dir. Demonstrate: tamper with a package/registry in the Worker-writable location and show collect still judges by the authoritative values.
acceptance_criteria: an example task completes the full Worker -> G2 -> commit -> PR flow with recorded evidence
a failed Worker never reaches accepted
a blocking test that is red prevents merge - demonstrated, not asserted
the Supervisor can resume an interrupted workflow from on-disk state alone
a RESULT claiming completed with a not_run required test is REJECTED at collect - demonstrated by planting one
the merge gate refuses when any of the six required CI jobs is not green - demonstrated
no file outside allowed_scope is modified
a Worker that widens its own allowed_scope or rewrites its recorded baseline_sha in its result dir is still judged by the authoritative gate inputs - demonstrated, not asserted
continuation: Attempt 1 exhausted $25 without writing any RESULT. Work is present and coherent; continue in the same worktree, verify it rather than rebuild it. go.mod/go.sum are now IN scope (the previous prohibition was stale - T0010 owned them and is merged).
